_meta.what: Key 2026 FIA Formula 1 regulation figures for car shape, mass and power. verified:true = read in the FIA PDF itself (text extracted from the fia.com file) in this session; quote is copied from it.

_meta.coordinates: Car Coordinate System (C2.1.1): X rearwards, Y to driver's right, Z up, mm. XF=0 / XR=0 = front / rear wheel-centre planes, XA=0 = front of survival cell, Z=0 = bottom of sprung car (plank excluded).
_meta.iss21_check: For each Issue 19 item, same_in_iss21 says whether Issue 21 (2026-10-19) has the same wording/number. Differences found: C5.2.10 ii (5 -> 4 MJ) and C5.2.8 iii (adds 'during any power limited period').

mass.quote: During the Sprint Qualifying and Qualifying sessions, The Minimum Mass is 726kg plus the Nominal Tyre Mass.
mass.note: Car without fuel is implied by the 768 kg figures in the press but the article itself does not mention fuel; Car Mass is a defined term in Section C.

mass.quote: In all other sessions, the Minimum Mass is 724kg plus the Nominal Tyre Mass.

the masses of new, production, dry weather, tyres will be measured by the tyre provider and published after the final day of TCC opportunity ... and will be the mean mass of sample of 50 tyres per axle.
mass.note: The value itself is published by Pirelli/FIA outside Section C and was not found. Press figure 768 kg total minimum (see reported_min_mass_total_kg) implies about 44 kg at 724 kg; that is arithmetic on a reported number, not a sourced value.
RacingNews365 uses 768 kg as the limit for its early-season team weight table. Not an FIA figure as read here.

mass.quote: the mass measured at the front axle must not be less than the Minimum Mass specified in Article C4.1 factored by 0.44.
mass.note: Applies during Qualifying and Sprint Qualifying. Front >= 0.44 and rear >= 0.54 leaves 0.02 of the minimum mass free to place.

mass.quote: the mass measured at the rear axle must not be less than the Minimum Mass specified in Article C4.1 factored by 0.54.
The reference Mass of the Driver plus the mass of any Driver Ballast must not be less than 82kg at any time during the Competition.
The Heat Hazard Mass Increase is 5kg.
The overall mass of the PU must be a minimum of 185 kg.
the total mass of the ICE must be no less than 130.0kg ... 134.0kg ... 132.0kg.
the total mass of the MGU-K must be no less than 20.0kg ... 16.0kg ... 18.0kg.
The minimum mass for the ES Main Enclosure PU Mass group elements as defined in Appendix C4 is 35.0kg.
The centre of gravity of the Power Unit must be above Z=200.

dimensions.quote: Except for the tyres, the Wheel Rims, and parts attached to the Wheel Rims as defined in Article C10.7.6, no part of the car may lie more than 950mm from the plane Y=0 at Legality Setup.
dimensions.note: So 1900 mm overall body width, tyres and rims excluded.

dimensions.quote: The distance between the planes XF = 0 and XR = 0 must be less than or equal to 3400mm at Legality Setup.

dimensions.unit: mm aft of XA=0 (front of survival cell)
dimensions.quote: The plane XF = 0 must lie between XA = 0 and XA = 150 inclusive.
The distance between XA = 0 and XC = 0 must be greater than or equal to 1830mm and less than or equal to 2030mm.
The origin of the front Wheel Coordinate System may not lie outboard of Y=603 when entering Parc Fermé.
dimensions.note: Wheel Coordinate System origin is on the inboard plane of the rim (C2.1.3 a), so this is not the tyre centreline.

dimensions.quote: The origin of the rear Wheel Coordinate System may not lie outboard of Y=525 when entering Parc Fermé.
The origin of the front Wheel Coordinate System may not lie outboard of Y=603 when entering Parc Fermé.
dimensions.note: Derived (this checklist): wheel centre plane = origin (inboard rim plane) + half the rim overall width (334 / 420.3 mm ref.), so track <= 2 x (603 + 167) = 1540 mm front and 2 x (525 + 210.15) = 1470.3 mm rear. The PhysicalCar uses 1.60 / 1.55 m (docs/concept/FIA_CHECKLIST.md, fix requested).

wheels_tyres.note: Table values front / rear columns; 18-inch nominal.

wheels_tyres.quote: Tyre specifications will be determined by the tyre supplier, in agreement with the FIA
wheels_tyres.note: Section C does not give tyre widths or diameters. Press reports (search-result summaries, articles not opened): front -25 mm and rear -30 mm width vs 2025, diameter 720 mm -> about 705-710 mm; a German source gives 305->275 mm front and 405->375 mm rear. Sources disagree; not confirmed.

aero.article: Appendix C2 §22 (RV-FW-PROFILES), used by C3.10.1 a
aero.quote: On a plane through XF = −1250, a simple, closed polygon ... [Y, Z] vertices ... [0, 60], [100, 60], [675, 115], [675, 275], [400, 300], [0, 200], [0,60]. ... extruded along X to XF = −475.
aero.note: Bounding box of the polygon; the volume is further trimmed by two planes (§22.3, §22.4). Y is per side, so span up to 1350 mm.

aero.quote: comprise of up to three, non-intersecting, simply connected volumes.

aero.article: Appendix C2 §30 (RV-RW-PROFILES), used by C3.11.1 a
aero.quote: An axis-aligned cuboid, which has one interior diagonal defined by the points: ... [XR = 165, 0, 725], [XR = 630, 575, 880].
aero.note: Then trimmed below a plane through [165,150,725], [165,575,785], [630,575,785]. Y per side, so span up to 1150 mm.

aero.quote: comprise of up to three, non-intersecting, simply connected volumes.

aero.value: FW Primary Flap and/or FW Secondary Flap rotate between two fixed positions: Corner Mode and Straight Mode (lower incidence)
aero.quote: a “Straight Mode” position that, when compared to the Corner Mode position, results in a decrease in incidence of FW Primary Flap and/or FW Secondary Flap.

aero.value: RW Flap rotates between Corner Mode and Straight Mode (lower incidence, fixed magnitude)
aero.quote: a “Straight Mode” position that, when compared to the Corner Mode position, results in a decrease in incidence of RW Flap. Furthermore, the magnitude of decrease must always remain identical.
have a maximum transition time between the two fixed positions that does not exceed 400ms
The design is such that failure of the system will result in RW Flap returning to its Corner Mode position.
the magnitude of decrease must always remain identical.
aero.note: The regulations fix that the Straight Mode change is constant but give no angle; it is the team's choice within the reference volume and physical stops.

aero.value: Full activation (front+rear in Straight Mode) only in FIA Activation Zones when enabled; in Low Grip Conditions only partial activation (front wing only) in Low Grip Activation Zones
aero.quote: In Low Grip Conditions, only partial activation of the Driver Adjustable Bodywork in the associated Low Grip Activation Zones is allowed.
On a plane through Y=0, a section whose edges pass through the following [X, Z] vertices sequentially: a. [XF = 1450, 275], [XF = 1450, 75], [XR = −600, 75], [XR = −350, 175], [XR = 300, 250].
aero.note: Upper trim sheet of the floor-body reference volume at the centreline (material above is discarded): flat at Z=75 to 600 mm ahead of the rear axle, then rising to Z=175 at XR-350 and Z=250 at XR+300. Reading this as the diffuser ramp envelope is an interpretation.
Plan outline of the floor body volume only; floor foot, sidewall and board volumes extend further outboard.

aero.quote: The thickness of the Plank Assembly measured normal to the lower surface must be 10mm ± 0.2mm and must be uniform when new. A minimum thickness of 8mm will be accepted due to wear
The upper surface of the Plank Assembly must lie at Z = 0
However, between three and five pairs of “Rear Wing Separators” must be fitted across both sides of the car. Each pair must:
aero.note: Each pair must intersect both the forwardmost volume of Rear Wing Profiles and RW Flap (b ii), and RW Flap excludes the forwardmost volume (C3.11.6 a i): a rear wing needs at least two volumes. regs.js REG-C-ELEMENTS-MIN.

aero.unit: mm [Y, Z] polygon, extruded along X
aero.note: Z height of RV-FW-PROFILES: 140 mm at Y=0, 211 mm at Y=400, 160 mm at Y=675; trims §22.3-22.4 are vertical planes. regs.js REG-C-FW-PROFILES-Z.

aero.quote: a “Straight Mode” position that, when compared to the Corner Mode position, results in a decrease in incidence of RW Flap.
aero.note: regs.js REG-C-SM-DIRECTION (a negative straight-mode delta is illegal).

aero.value: C3.11.1 not applied to RW Flap adjustments
aero.quote: compliance with all bodywork regulations except for Article C3.11.1.
aero.note: So the rear flap may leave RV-RW-PROFILES in Straight Mode; the front flaps may not (C3.10.10 s i).

aero.quote: The centres must lie on Y = 0 and have X-locations XF = 500, −600 ≥ XC ≥ −800, and 470 ≤ XPU ≤ 630. Furthermore, the centre of the rearmost hole must lie on or ahead of XR = −500.
aero.note: Implies XR - XPU >= 970 mm. regs.js REG-C-PLANK-HOLES.

aero.quote: C3.16.9 Sidepod [20, 475, 250] 80,000 Front i. Must lie in its entirety above Z = 275.
aero.note: Aperture table row (area column, per side per C3.16 d). regs.js REG-C-SIDEPOD-INLET (concept inlet_cm2 is both sides, <= 1600 cm2).

aero.quote: The material of the Plank is free, but it must be homogeneous with a specific gravity between 1.3 and 1.45

power_unit.quote: Engine cubic capacity must be 1600cc (+0/−10cc). ... All engines must have six cylinders arranged in a 90° “V” configuration
Fuel energy flow must not exceed 3000MJ/h, with a maximum energy flow per cylinder never exceeding 550MJ/h under normal operating conditions.
power_unit.note: 3000 MJ/h = 833 kW of fuel energy (derived: /3.6). ICE shaft power then depends on efficiency, which the rules do not fix.

power_unit.quote: Below 10500rpm the fuel energy flow must not exceed EF(MJ/h)=0.27*N(rpm)+ 165

power_unit.note: No ICE power cap exists in Section C; output is limited through fuel energy flow (C5.2.3). formula1.com's explainer gives only the target of about 50 per cent electric power; no official ICE kW figure was found.

power_unit.quote: The absolute electrical DC power of the ERS-K may not exceed 350kW.
P(kW) = 1800 – 5 * car speed (kph) when the car speed is below 340kph
power_unit.note: 1800-5v reaches 350 kW at v = 290 km/h, so full 350 kW is available up to 290 km/h (derived).

power_unit.quote: P(kW) = 7100 – 20 * car speed (kph) when the car speed is below 355kph

power_unit.value: P = 250 kW below 310 km/h, then the base taper
power_unit.quote: P(kW) = 250 when the car speed is below 310kph
power_unit.note: Applies in Race/Sprint on FIA-specified sectors (at Silverstone: T1-T4 350-1000 m, T15-T16 4950-5450 m per the PU information doc). Issue 21 adds 'during any power limited period'.

power_unit.quote: The difference between the maximum and the minimum state of charge of the ES may not exceed 4MJ at any time the car is on the track.
Recharge, as measured at the CU-K HV DC Bus, must not exceed a limit of 8.5MJ in each lap
power_unit.note: May be reduced to 7 MJ at some events (i); Q/SQ may go down to 5 MJ in Issue 19 (ii), changed to 4 MJ in Issue 21; +0.5 MJ with Overtake (iii). Silverstone values: 8.0 MJ race/sprint without Overtake, 8.5 with, 6.5 MJ in SQ/Q (fia_gbr_pu_info).

power_unit.quote: This limit may be further reduced to no less than 5MJ for Sprint Qualifying and Qualifying sessions
power_unit.note: Issue 21 (19 Oct 2026) strikes 5 and writes 4 MJ (seen in the marked-up PDF).

power_unit.quote: Up to 0.5MJ of additional energy may be harvested in each lap subject to the conditions specified in Article B7.2.
The MGU-K mechanical torque magnitude may not exceed 500Nm.
During a standing start from the grid the MGU-K may only be used once the car has reached 50 km/h.

power_unit.note: No per-lap deployment cap appears in C5.2; deployment is bounded by the 350 kW / speed curves, the 4 MJ state-of-charge window and per-lap Recharge.

power_unit.quote: The rotational speed of the Turbo Charger may not exceed 150,000rpm.
The Maximum Working Voltage on the car must never exceed 1000V.

fuel.value: Advanced Sustainable (AS) fuels comprising solely AS components
fuel.quote: the detailed requirements of this Article are intended to ensure the use of Advanced Sustainable (AS) fuels comprising solely AS components

fuel.note: No maximum race fuel mass was found in Section C Issue 19 or Section B Issue 07 (searched for fuel with kg/MJ). Not confirmed either way.

materials.quote: No parts of the car may be made from metallic materials that have a specific modulus of elasticity greater than 40 GPa/(g/cm3).
materials.note: Beryllium (287 GPa / 1.85) = 155, AlBeMet = 93: prohibited. regs.js REG-C-MAT-SPECIFIC-MODULUS.

materials.quote: Materials used in the construction of the Formula One car – excluding the Power Unit − are limited to those defined in article C15.2 and to the specific exceptions in article C15.4.

Carbon fibres manufactured from polyacrylonitrile (PAN) precursor, which have: − A nominal tensile modulus ≤ 550GPa − A nominal tensile strength ≤ 7100 MPa (i.e. up to and including that of Toray T1100 or Mitsubishi MR70) − A density ≤ 1.92 g/cm3
UNS M18432, WE43B ii. UNS M18434, WE43C iii. UNS M18410, WE54A iv. UNS M11800, AZ80A
Copper Alloys containing less than 2.5% Beryllium
Particulate Reinforced Aluminium Alloy Matrix Composite i. SupremEX 225XE ii. SupremEX 225XF
Shape Memory Materials except for piezoelectric materials used in electrical sensors.
Wheel Rims must be made from AZ70 or AZ80 magnesium alloy.
The Heat Exchanger Core and header tanks must be made from aluminium alloy.
Unless explicitly permitted for a specific application, the following materials may not be used on the Power Unit: a. Magnesium based alloys.
Material with a density exceeding 18,400 kg/m3.
